Why Gandhi chose salt for Civil Disobedience: the Salt March, Class 10 History, Nationalism in India, explained.

• Salt was eaten by rich and poor alike, and the government's monopoly over it showed the most oppressive face of British rule
• Non-Cooperation refused to cooperate; Civil Disobedience also broke colonial laws
• The Salt March: 78 volunteers, over 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi in 24 days
• 6 April: salt made from boiling sea water at Dandi, and the Civil Disobedience Movement began
